142	\paragraph{The structural mismatch.}
143	The key observation is that factor (b) makes the KL gradient for neuron $j$ depend on \emph{all} other neurons' mask values.
144	BCE's factorized gradient (Eq.~\ref{eq:bce_grad}) optimizes each neuron's prediction accuracy in isolation, but TEAL inference selects neurons via a global ranking across all layers.

The advantage concentrates in early layers (0--4: ratio $34$--$156\times$) where factor~(b)'s Jacobian chain traverses the full remaining network; late layers (27--31: $1.7$--$3.8\times$) show reduced advantage as the shorter chain limits factor~(b)'s contribution.
BCE's early-layer SNR collapses to ${\sim}10^{-8}$ after step~10, consistent with (though not exclusively explained by) rapid convergence of the per-neuron classification task; an alternative explanation is that BCE gradients vanish once per-neuron accuracy plateaus (loss saturation rather than signal quality).
This 80-step measurement is preliminary; the pattern persists regardless of learning rate, but a complete characterization across the full training trajectory is left to future work.

9	DejaVu~\cite{liu2023dejavu} introduced learned sparsity predictors trained via BCE to classify each neuron independently.
